data.content_ref: inline:The claim asserts decentralized networks are 'fundamentally less resilient' yet provides no causal mechanism connecting 'constant low-level churn' to lower resilience against CORRELATED failure—the exact phenomenon the problem asks about. The mechanism only argues reduced quality-of-service from frequent partial outages, which is orthogonal to resilience under correlated stress. Under a correlated shock (e.g., shared dependency failure), the large service's internal redundancy offers no protection if the shared subsystem fails, while geographically/logically separated small services may survive; the target never addresses this. Its own countercondition concedes total collapse is avoided in the decentralized case, undermining the claim that it is 'fundamentally less resilient.' The argument conflates availability with correlated-failure resilience without bridging the two.
